methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier is a seed-stage transportation company that has raised $7.2M to date. The transportation sector comp universe includes six private peers—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, EarthGrid, and Olympian Motors—though no public comparables are available and same-stage private peers are limited.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $7.2M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to advance from Seed to Series A. This approach yields an implied valuation of $18M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer density: while three transportation-sector companies exist in the broader comp set, none meet the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier placement, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold needed for reliable median calculation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $21M, with a median point estimate of $18M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result. The primary uncertainty is the absence of directly comparable seed-stage transportation companies in available datasets, which limits cross-validation of the stage-progression step-up multiplier. Investors should treat this analysis as anchored to one method and remain alert to company-specific execution risks and market-cycle timing in the transportation sector.
